newsitem.title: USA: Central Newspapers to close Phoenix Gazette.
newsitem.headline: Central Newspapers to close Phoenix Gazette.

text.p: The 116-year-old Phoenix Gazette, an afternoon newspaper, will close on Jan. 18, and owner Central Newspapers Inc. said Monday it will cut 85 jobs at the morning Arizona Republic.
The 85 positions will be eliminated in the news and circulation operations, Central Newspapers said.

Indianapolis-based Central Newspapers said it planned to expand the Arizona Republic's local news coverage, raise performance standards for journalists, use new pagination and text-handling technology and prepare new editorial products and sections.
The Phoenix Gazette was founded as a morning paper Oct. 28, 1880, when Phoenix was 11 years old. It was the city's oldest continuously operated newspaper.

The Arizona Republic, with a circulation of 389,000 daily and 553,000 Sunday, is one of the fastest growing newspapers in the country while the Phoenix Gazette has seen a steady dwindling of its circulation to the current level of 38,000, the company said.

"After an extensive evaluation of the Phoenix and Arizona markets, the Phoenix management team concluded that the overall market they cover would be better served by one newspaper," Louis Weil, chief executive officer of Central Newspapers, said in a statement.

"The closing of the afternoon newspaper should be considered as one part of a larger shift in our Phoenix resources in order to gather news better, present it better and provide a better service to our readers," Weil said. "We will be able to concentrate our resources and energy on continuing the growth of the morning and Sunday Republic."
As a result of the planned actions, the company said it planned to take a one-time charge in the first quarter of 1997 of $4.2 million to $4.8 million.
Central Newspapers also publishes The Indianapolis Star, The Indianapolis News, Muncie Star and community newspapers.
Central Newspaper's stock rose $2.25 to $46.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
